I will keep my planting simple and familiar, because at 70 I value a steady harvest more than chasing complicated changes. In Quzhou County, the wheat-maize rotation fits my land, my labor, and the local water and weather best, so I will stay with that as the main pattern. I will plant winter wheat on all my fields first, then follow with summer maize after wheat harvest. I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed because I want better stability and disease resistance, but I will avoid overly expensive or management-heavy choices. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage and matches the machinery I can realistically handle. On fertilizer, I will apply enough nitrogen to secure yield, but I will not push it too high because that raises cost and lodging risk; I will keep phosphorus and potassium at moderate levels to support roots, grain filling, and soil balance. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, because wheat in my area usually needs more careful water management through overwintering, jointing, and grain filling, while maize can rely more on summer rainfall with some supplemental watering if needed. I will spray pesticides only when pressure is likely, keeping wheat to a few treatments for weeds, aphids, and disease, and maize to a small number for borers, armyworms, and leaf diseases. My goal is not the absolute highest yield; my goal is a dependable year with manageable labor, controlled cost, and low risk.
